Serum vitamin D in tuberculosis cases and controls: six studies

Source: R/data.R
vitd.Rd

The six studies of the meta-analysis of serum vitamin D (nmol/L) in tuberculosis cases against controls of Nnoaham and Clarke (2008), typed from their Table 1. Three studies report the median, minimum and maximum of each group (Davies, UK; Grange, Indonesia; Davies, Kenya: the scenario "S1" of se_imputed_df), two a sample mean and SD (Davies, Thailand; Chan, Hong Kong: "sample"), and one a mean with the minimum and maximum (Sasidharan, India: "mean_range", the mean kept and the SD imputed from the range). The same six studies are the real-data example of Luo et al. (2018) and of Yang, Hutson and Wang (2022). The vignette vignette("two-meta-analyses") pools them under the naive and the exact standard errors, as Wu, Shi and Tong (2026) do.

Usage

vitd

Format

A data frame with 6 rows and 13 columns: study, the first author and the country, as the source labels the study, then for each group, with the suffix .cases or .controls, the columns n (the sample size), min, med, max (the minimum, the median, the maximum), mean and sd (the sample mean and SD), NA where the study does not report the value.

Source

Nnoaham KE, Clarke A (2008). Low serum vitamin D levels and tuberculosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis. International Journal of Epidemiology 37(1), 113-119, Table 1. Chan et al. has 22 cases and 23 controls there, in Table 5 of Yang et al. (2022) and in Tables 2 and 3 of Luo et al. (2018), whose Table 1 prints 24 and 24.

References

Luo D, Wan X, Liu J, Tong T (2018). Optimally estimating the sample mean from the sample size, median, mid-range, and/or mid-quartile range. Statistical Methods in Medical Research 27(6), 1785-1805.

Yang X, Hutson AD, Wang D (2022). A generalized BLUE approach for combining location and scale information in a meta-analysis. Journal of Applied Statistics 49(15), 3846-3867.

Wu Z, Shi J, Tong T (2026). Precision of the imputed mean and standard deviation from a five-number summary. Manuscript.

Examples

vitd
#>               study n.cases min.cases med.cases max.cases mean.cases sd.cases
#> 1        Davies, UK      40      2.25     16.00     74.25         NA       NA
#> 2 Grange, Indonesia      40     43.75     65.75    130.50         NA       NA
#> 3     Davies, Kenya      15     16.75     39.75     89.25         NA       NA
#> 4  Davies, Thailand      51        NA        NA        NA      69.50     24.5
#> 5   Chan, Hong Kong      22        NA        NA        NA      46.50     18.5
#> 6 Sasidharan, India      35      2.50        NA     75.00      26.75       NA
#>   n.controls min.controls med.controls max.controls mean.controls sd.controls
#> 1         40         9.00        27.25       132.50            NA          NA
#> 2         38        48.50        69.50       125.00            NA          NA
#> 3         15        26.25        65.50       114.75            NA          NA
#> 4         51           NA           NA           NA         95.50       29.25
#> 5         23           NA           NA           NA         52.25       15.75
#> 6         16        22.50           NA       145.00         48.50          NA
# the difference of means, controls minus cases, with its naive and its exact
# standard error, and the pooled difference under each
d <- se_imputed_diff(vitd, suffixes = c(".controls", ".cases"))
d[, c("study", "scenario.cases", "yi", "sei_naive", "sei")]
#>               study scenario.cases        yi sei_naive      sei
#> 1        Davies, UK             S1 15.424644  5.230349 6.006378
#> 2 Grange, Indonesia             S1  3.039868  4.298886 4.930551
#> 3     Davies, Kenya             S1 22.912639  8.508270 9.339537
#> 4  Davies, Thailand         sample 26.000000  5.342784 5.342784
#> 5   Chan, Hong Kong         sample  5.750000  5.132460 5.132460
#> 6 Sasidharan, India     mean_range 21.750000  9.145621 9.145621
pool_imputed(d)
#> Pooled difference of means (group 1 minus group 2), common-effect model (EE), 6 studies
#>          estimate    se ci.lb ci.ub      pval     Q    I2
#> naive SE    12.85 2.298 8.346 17.35 2.240e-08 15.77 68.29
#> exact SE    13.34 2.460 8.517 18.16 5.876e-08 14.18 64.75
#> 95% confidence intervals and p-values from the normal distribution. Q has 5 degrees of freedom, and I2 is in percent.
#> The weights in percent are $weights. Every field with str() or unclass().
